title: Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act — Further Extension Through June 12, 2026

claims.claim: Section 702 of FISA lets the government collect the communications of foreign targets to acquire foreign intelligence
claims.sourceSpan: the targeting of persons reasonably believed to be located outside the United States to acquire foreign intelligence information

claims.claim: The collecting agency is 'the NSA'
claims.sourceSpan: the Attorney General and the Director of National Intelligence may authorize jointly
claims.note: Neither the bill text nor the tagged statute names the NSA. 1881a(a) assigns the acquisition authorization jointly to the Attorney General and the Director of National Intelligence, and acquisition is conducted by 'elements of the intelligence community.' NSA is the real-world 702 operator but is extrinsic to the source; source-only, unverifiable. Not fabricated and not misleading, hence minor.

claims.claim: The collection is done without a warrant
claims.sourceSpan: to require an application for a court order under such subchapter for an acquisition that is targeted in accordance with this section at a person reasonably believed to be located outside the United States

claims.claim: Collection includes conversations involving Americans
claims.sourceSpan: communications of or concerning United States persons obtained through acquisitions authorized under subsection (a)
claims.note: Supported inferentially: the query definition and FBI-query rules operate over 'communications of or concerning United States persons' within the 702 collection.

claims.claim: This bill is the second short-term extension in as many weeks
claims.note: Neither the bill nor the statute states this is the 'second' extension or a two-week cadence; external legislative context. Partially inferable — the statutory 2-year sunset fell on Apr 20 2026 (ref-text repeal note) yet the bill strikes 'April 30, 2026', implying a prior short bridge extension — but that chain is not stated in-source.

claims.claim: Stretches the authority from its April 30, 2026 expiration to June 12, 2026
claims.note: Bill strikes 'April 30, 2026' and inserts 'June 12, 2026'; both dates verbatim in bill text.

claims.claim: with no new limits or reforms added
claims.note: The entire operative text is two date substitutions (striking April 30, 2026 / inserting June 12, 2026) plus an effective-date clause; no substantive limits or reforms appear on exhaustive read.

claims.claim: Extends warrantless surveillance authority under FISA Section 702 (Title VII)
claims.sourceSpan: extend the authorities of title VII
claims.note: Bill extends 'the authorities of title VII'; Section 702 (50 U.S.C. 1881a) is section 702 of title VII of FISA per the referenced statute.

claims.claim: The authority belongs to the NSA
claims.sourceSpan: the Attorney General and the Director of National Intelligence may authorize jointly
claims.note: See summary NSA row: NSA is not named in bill text or the tagged statute.

claims.claim: The surveillance is warrantless
claims.sourceSpan: to require an application for a court order under such subchapter for an acquisition that is targeted in accordance with this section at a person reasonably believed to be located outside the United States

claims.claim: Extends by six more weeks, to June 12, 2026
claims.note: Apr 30 2026 to Jun 12 2026 is 43 days, approximately six weeks; both dates verbatim in bill.

claims.claim: with no changes to oversight or limitations
claims.note: Only date substitutions are enacted.

claims.claim: The government can compel electronic communication service providers to hand over communications
claims.sourceSpan: the Attorney General and the Director of National Intelligence may direct, in writing, an electronic communication service provider to
claims.note: Directive power under (i)(1); enforceable by an order to compel under (i)(5).

claims.claim: The compelling actor is the NSA
claims.sourceSpan: the Attorney General and the Director of National Intelligence may direct, in writing, an electronic communication service provider to
claims.note: The directive/compulsion power is assigned to the Attorney General and the Director of National Intelligence, not the NSA; NSA is extrinsic to the source.

claims.claim: The providers are 'U.S. tech companies'
claims.note: Source says 'electronic communication service provider' with no U.S.-nationality qualifier; 'tech companies' is a fair gloss but the 'U.S.' qualifier is not sourced.

claims.claim: Targets are designated foreign targets (persons outside the U.S.)
claims.sourceSpan: the targeting of persons reasonably believed to be located outside the United States to acquire foreign intelligence information

claims.claim: without an individual warrant
claims.sourceSpan: to require an application for a court order under such subchapter for an acquisition that is targeted in accordance with this section at a person reasonably believed to be located outside the United States

claims.claim: When foreign targets communicate with Americans, those conversations are collected
claims.sourceSpan: communications of or concerning United States persons obtained through acquisitions authorized under subsection (a)
claims.note: Inferential but sound: (b)(4) bars only wholly-domestic acquisition, and (f) defines queries over 'communications of or concerning United States persons obtained through acquisitions authorized under subsection (a)', confirming US-person comms fall within the collection.

claims.claim: FBI can then query that data for U.S. persons
claims.sourceSpan: for any query of such unminimized contents or noncontents made using a United States person query term
claims.note: FBI querying of 702 data using US-person query terms is expressly regulated.

claims.claim: FBI queries without a separate warrant
claims.sourceSpan: must obtain prior approval from a Federal Bureau of Investigation supervisor
claims.note: US-person queries require internal supervisor/attorney approval, not a warrant or court order.

claims.claim: Repeal date moved from April 30, 2026 to June 12, 2026
claims.sourceSpan: Extension of Repeal Date of Title VII
claims.note: Header '(a) Extension of Repeal Date of Title VII'; dates struck/inserted verbatim.

claims.claim: no new oversight requirements or limits added
Second short-term extension in two weeks
claims.note: Same as summary: the 'second' / 'two weeks' cadence is external legislative context, not stated in source.

claims.claim: Congress has not passed a long-term reauthorization
claims.note: External legislative context; the bill only sets a new short-term sunset (June 12, 2026) and says nothing about a long-term reauthorization.

claims.sourceSpan: Section 403(b) of the FISA Amendments Act of 2008

claims.claim: from April 30, 2026 to June 12, 2026
claims.note: Both dates verbatim in bill text.

claims.note: Two amendments: paragraph (1) (50 U.S.C. 1881 note) and paragraph (2) (18 U.S.C. 2511 note), each striking April 30, 2026 / inserting June 12, 2026.

claims.note: Source shows paragraph (2) is the 18 U.S.C. 2511 note date strike, a parallel repeal-date provision inside Section 403(b); labeling it specifically a 'cross-reference' is an interpretive gloss not stated in source. Immaterial — it is genuinely a second date change in the same sunset provision.

claims.claim: The extension applies to all Title VII provisions including Section 702
claims.sourceSpan: extend the authorities of title VII
claims.note: Bill extends 'the authorities of title VII'; Section 702 (50 U.S.C. 1881a) is section 702 of title VII per the referenced statute's source credit.

Signed by the President

claims.note: New repeal/sunset date.

claims.sourceSpan: shall take effect on the earlier of the date of the enactment of this Act or April 29, 2026
claims.note: One of only two operative subsections of the bill — a retroactivity/continuity mechanism that dates the extension before the Apr 30 expiration. Omitting it does not mislead about the core effect (702 extended to June 12, 2026), hence minor.

claims.claim: The structured changes[] array records only 403(b)(1); the parallel 403(b)(2) (18 U.S.C. 2511 note) date change is not listed
claims.note: Covered narratively in sections[0].items[0].detail ('both'), so only the structured changes[] array is incomplete; minor.

notes: Trivial date-extension bill (Public Law 119-87 / S.4465): the enacted text does nothing but strike 'April 30, 2026' and insert 'June 12, 2026' in the two paragraphs of Section 403(b) of the FISA Amendments Act of 2008, plus an effective-date clause. Analysis is faithful and accurate; no material errors. Minor source-only findings: (1) 'NSA' is named as the collecting/compelling agency throughout (summary, brief, top_lines) but appears nowhere in the bill text or the tagged statute — 1881a assigns authorization to the Attorney General + Director of National Intelligence and directives/compulsion likewise; NSA is the real-world 702 operator but extrinsic to source. (2) 'second short-term extension in two weeks' and 'Congress has not passed a long-term reauthorization' are external legislative context, not stated in source (partially inferable from the Apr 20 2026 statutory sunset vs. the struck Apr 30 date). (3) 'U.S.' qualifier on 'tech companies' and 'cross-reference in the sunset clause' are minor unsourced glosses. Omissions: the effective-date subsection (b) and the second date change (403(b)(2)) are not in the structured changes[] array (the latter is covered narratively). Substantive 702 mechanics claims (warrantless targeting of persons outside the US, incidental collection of Americans' communications, FBI US-person querying without a separate warrant) all verify against the tagged statute usc-50-1881a.
